name: TN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district lean of R+11
Incumbent DesJarlais has large financial advantage
Democratic challenger Broderick raised only $60K with $8.5K on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, DesJarlais's incumbency and roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Republican win near certainty all point to a comfortable Republican hold with little evidence of Democratic strength.
model.watch: Any late polling or a surge in outside spending against DesJarlais could tighten the race, but no such evidence exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott DesJarlais seeks another term in a southern Tennessee district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over half a million dollars and holding nearly $500,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Victoria Broderick has raised under $60,000 with minimal cash remaining. Two independent candidates are on the ballot but show little fundraising activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets give the Republican side roughly a 94 percent chance of winning. With no evidence of a competitive environment, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a solid double-digit margin, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
